mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment rate increases above 0.3pp for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and acceleration of inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% signals a robust recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months when housing starts increase by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two consecutive months indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which dampens consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses retail and discretionary equities and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12mo MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
